assumptions: THIS INCREMENT IS BATCH 102, A FORWARD FIX IN 094's SHAPE: updated_by is in the INSERT grant to authenticated on thirteen client-writable tables and was checked on UPDATE everywhere and on INSERT nowhere, so a row's first updater could be anybody until its first real update -- the LOW siblings A1-090 S13 named beside requested_by.

ONE RESTRICTIVE INSERT POLICY PER TABLE, `updated_by is null or updated_by = (select auth.uid())`, ANDed with each table's permissive policy. NULL is admitted and stated as the one difference from 094: a row never updated has no updater, and the triggers 093 maintains write updated_at, not updated_by.

A SCHEMA-WIDE APPLY-TIME ASSERTION names any table that grants updated_by at INSERT without a restrictive INSERT policy binding it, so the next batch that repeats the shape fails at apply time by table name rather than by a reviewer noticing.
NUMBERED 102 BECAUSE IT NAMES app.assets: 095 failed to apply (the table did not exist yet); the file sorts after 101 and before 110, and the not-applied tail stays contiguous.

security_privacy_cost_impact: Closes the LOW half of A1-090 S13: a client can no longer write another member's id as a row's first updated_by on thirteen tables. Adds no grant and no read surface; thirteen RESTRICTIVE policies that only narrow. The audit value of updated_by -- who last touched a row -- was forgeable at INSERT and is not now.
migration_and_data_impact: Thirteen RESTRICTIVE INSERT policies and one apply-time assertion; no table, column, grant or trigger. Existing rows are untouched (a policy binds writes, not history). No fixture writes updated_by at INSERT as somebody else; measured by the full set still loading.
compatibility_impact: A client that inserts a row may leave updated_by NULL or set it to its own auth.uid(); any other value is refused 42501 as the permissive policy's row would have been. Nothing in the repository writes another value except the two new cases.
known_limitations: NULL updated_by at INSERT is admitted, so "who created this row" is answered by created_by where a table has it and by nothing where it does not; this batch binds the column it was asked about and does not invent a creator column.
The apply-time assertion reads the policy text for auth.uid(); a restrictive policy that named the function inside a comment would pass it. The two cases are the control behind the text.
open_risks_or_blockers: None opened. A1-090 S13 (the HIGH half, requested_by) was closed by 094; this batch closes the LOW siblings it named.
rollback_or_forward_fix: Revert the merge commit: thirteen policies and the assertion go; updated_by at INSERT becomes forgeable again on thirteen tables, which is the state A1-090 S13 recorded.
recommended_next_work_packages: The pre-080 families closures once the Owner picks a row of the S8 map (a0-pre-080-families-s8-map-2026-09-15.md).
reviewer_instructions: Apply the set on a scratch PostgreSQL with and without 102_updated_by_is_caller.sql and run rls-smoke: exactly the two new cases must fail without it with "1 row(s) came back" and pass with it.
Count the tables that grant updated_by to authenticated at INSERT (thirteen) against the thirteen policies; the apply-time block does the same count and names any table it misses.
Compare the predicate with 094's: the only difference is `updated_by is null or`, and the header says why.
